page_content: The page considers exactly two strata: a closed X_0 and its complement X_1. It attributes to Artin a description of a sheaf F by two restricted sheaves and a map F_0 to i_0^*i_{1*}(F_1).

It states a constructibility criterion in terms of local constancy, with additional finiteness conditions acknowledged only briefly. It then states that equisingularity gives the same local-constancy property for the comparison functor.

The revised passage expresses the relevant category in terms of locally constant sheaves, hence the mere homotopy types of the strata, while requiring the nature of the left-exact functor φ still to be specified.

It proposes an étale tubular neighbourhood of X_0 in X in the schematic setting, described as a topos not associated with a scheme. The page ends midword at para-; nothing from the next page was read or supplied.

notes.page_date_title_evidence: Author number 29 is at the top centre. Archive pencil 174 is at the lower left. This is a continuation of the handwritten letter; there is no date, title, salutation, closing, or signature on this sheet.
notes.layout: One continuous prose block. The indent of L7–8 accommodates the independent marginal diagram; a new sentence alone was not treated as a paragraph break. All mathematical expressions outside the diagram are inline.
notes.math_triggered_reading_decisions: The restriction formulas and the later composite were examined for index, star, prime, and direction consistency. Source/target consistency supports the preferred composite but does not decide the uncertain ink. No sign was silently repaired to fit the argument.
notes.mathematical_check_scope: Only the explicitly recorded local source/target check was performed. No proof of the asserted gluing description, equisingularity claim, homotopy-type dependence, or proposed tubular-neighbourhood construction was attempted.
notes.nontext_marks: No independent separator stroke or coherent isolated nontext point was established beyond the recorded cancellation, underlining, and attachment strokes. Border/copy lines and isolated grain were not promoted to manuscript marks.
notes.end_of_page: The visible para- is kept as the page-final fragment. The difference between a retained line-end hyphen and C's para% continuation convention is not counted as a substantive collation difference.
notes.H_editorial_notes: H's notes were used only to locate its claims. In particular, the asserted ordering from an English version was not evidence for the reading; the insertion order was read from the ink and attachment.

No global hypothesis or theorem was checked.

workflow_feedback: The brief was sufficient to finish this page independently. For future collation, a fixed marked_in_H policy for a symbol whose uncertainty is acknowledged only in an editorial note would make counts more uniform.
The ambiguous split word at L22–23 required two distant tight crops, one per physical segment; both were displayed once. No expanded half or re-crop was used.
The current clarification on physical placement versus inferred chronology is useful for the layered L15 cancellation; the report retains uncertainty where descenders and underlying ink overlap.
